subject: Rapid rejection blitz — Clearsight capacity failover & exec update
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha.rao@clearsight.ai>

Cc: support@clearsight.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 17:12:03 -0800
Subject: sudden spike in 429s + tail-latency (production)

Hi Sofia —

We're seeing a very sharp spike in 429s and 5xx tail latency starting ~16:50 PST. Affected endpoints are our high-priority inference routes (model: gpt-1b-clarity). Errors jump when we cross ~18k concurrent tokens/minute. This didn't happen in prior load tests.

We've attached a small log bundle and the aggregated charts. We need help understanding whether this is a policy misconfiguration on our account (quota/burst window) or something on Redwood's end. Clearsight is in production for a big feature launch tomorrow; this is critical.

Attachments: clearsight_metrics_1124.zip (log bundle)

Can someone triage and propose an immediate mitigation (short-lived) — we can accept a temporary rate lift for the next 6 hours if that helps. Please loop in whoever owns quota/burst rules.

Thanks,
Asha

Asha — thanks for the flag and the logs. I'm escalating to ops and spin-up on our side now. Quick plan: 

- Monica (runtime) will validate whether the tenant mapping bumped Clearsight into the smaller burst window profile (common migration bug).
- Jonas (infra) will check capacity saturation and immediate route-failover possibilities (canary to a compatible model variant).
- Karthik (sales) will coordinate customer communication and confirm whether Clearsight can tolerate a temporary burst lift/credit.

Immediate mitigation asks for Clearsight: if you can momentarily switch traffic to a slightly lower max-concurrency key or enable a fallback route, that will reduce token peaks while we map the policy. We'll treat this as P1.

Runbook link: https://drive.redwood.ai/rdw-runbooks/throttle-failover

I'm on a short bridge with the team. Marissa — I'd like an exec-level one-line to Asha and a proposed credit/comp plan if policy rollback is required.

Sofia

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

On Tue, Nov 24, 2026 at 5:12 PM Asha Rao <asha.rao@clearsight.ai> wrote:
> We're seeing a very sharp spike in 429s and 5xx tail latency starting ~16:50 PST...

Quick technical read: I pulled the policy snapshot and the snapshot shows Clearsight's account was incorrectly mapped to the "standard-burst-v2" window after yesterday's policy roll (compare to policy_snapshot_20261124.json). The standard-burst-v2 has a much shorter burst replenishment interval and a more aggressive token burn rate for identical sustained traffic; that fits the symptom of rapid rejection as requests cross short-term peaks.

Immediate actions I pushed (temporary, low-risk):
- Rolled back tenant->policy mapping to "standard-burst-v1" for Clearsight (effective now).
- Opened a targeted bypass to allow short-lived burst credits while we watch (6h window)
- Jonas is re-routing 5% of traffic to a compatible model variant (gpt-1b-clarity-lite) to reduce pressure on the main pool.

Monitoring: internal dashboards now show rejection rate dropping; Asha, please confirm on your end.

Next steps for RCA: capture kernel selection traces for the time window, correlate with the policy-deploy change at 12:03 UTC, and size whether this requires a config fix or a rollback of the deployment pipeline. I'll prepare a remediation PR for runtime policy normalization and include smoke tests in the rollout gate.

Attachments: policy_snapshot_20261124.json

Monica
Monica Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha.rao@clearsight.ai>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden spike in 429s + tail-latency (production) — exec summary

Asha — following Sofia's note, Monica and Jonas implemented a temporary rollback and a targeted route failover which has reduced the 429 spike. Early telemetry shows rejections down ~78% and tail latency improving. We're keeping the temporary burst lift (6 hours) while monitoring and will close the window if any regressions occur.

Our commitments: 
- We will own the RCA and share a written postmortem within 72 hours that includes the policy config change that caused the regression, corrective pipeline gating, and regression tests.
- If the RCA shows the policy rollout caused customer impact, we'll credit Clearsight for the token overage during the 6-hour mitigation window (details via Karthik).
- We'll schedule a 30-minute exec sync for tomorrow 10:00 AM PST to walk through timeline and confirm remediation.

Thank you for the quick flag — we appreciate the partnership while we fix this.

Marissa Cole
